title: Green health check, broken requests

cast.name: Tess
cast.role: Curious junior engineer who states the plausible wrong assumption

cast.name: Omar
cast.role: Calm staff engineer who asks for evidence and explains the mechanism

glossary.full: A partial or subtle failure perceived differently by different parts of a system
glossary.note: Research describes this as differential observability.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Interview drill. Tess sees a green health check while a customer’s database-backed read stalls.

visuals.text: illustrative path; not an incident report

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: The monitor sees healthy, so every caller must be fine.

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: What does it exercise? Here, it answers locally without querying the database.

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: The caller’s read can still wait on the database while that probe succeeds?

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: Yes. That partial mismatch is gray failure: one observer sees success while the user-facing path is impaired.

visuals.text: monitor sees success; caller sees impairment

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: One average latency number should tell me which callers and routes are affected.

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: Slice errors and tail latency by route, zone, shard, and caller. Compare the probe with the failing path.

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: Would restarting every ready service fix a slow database dependency?

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: Readiness proves only its configured test passed. Synchronized restarts can add load; find the failing dependency first.

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: What evidence can I add without creating more pressure on that dependency?

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: Use bounded representative reads from relevant caller locations, with route-level errors and latency. Limit probes so they do not add pressure.

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: I will add a bounded read probe from the customer’s location. That green dashboard needs a second witness.

key_points: Gray failure means different system components can perceive a failure differently.
A shallow health endpoint can succeed while a user-facing dependency path is impaired.
Compare bounded representative probes and caller-side route signals by vantage point and dependency.
